rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier flood-and-froth parable depicts froth disappearing, leaving the Qur’an and those who receive it.
rows.anchor: very soon all this froth will vanish and whatever remains is the Qur’ān and its recipients.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence suppresses an explanation: God gives parables so falsehood’s supporters see their fate and believers see their bright fate.
rows.anchor: Some words after “God in this manner relates parables” are suppressed. The overall sentence would be:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted noun qualified by al-ḥusnā is al-ʿāqibat al-ḥusnā, meaning the good fate, understood from context.
rows.anchor: has been suppressed here because of concomitant indications.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 18 restates in plain terms the good outcome represented by the earlier parable.
rows.anchor: What is said in the form of a parable earlier is stated here in simple words.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harsh accountability means even slight blemishes are punished and every utterance and deed appears in its original horrific form.
rows.anchor: the slightest of their blemishes will be punished and every utterance and deed of theirs will come before them in its original horrific form.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers’ mistakes are overlooked, whereas even the smallest deeds of arrogant people will loom like mountains.
rows.anchor: their blemishes and mistakes will be ignored but as for these arrogant individuals, even their most minute deeds will appear as mountains.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love of worldly possessions is the real reason people evade the Qur’an’s message, yet those possessions cannot ransom them in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: it is the love of the material world that is stopping them to accept the message of the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Blind” means blindness of heart and intellect, as it did in verse 16.
rows.anchor: The word “blind” here refers to blindness of the heart and intellect. In verse 16 too, it has been used thus.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reassures the Prophet while admonishing disbelievers: only people of intellect receive his reminder, so he need not be needlessly dejected.
rows.anchor: The verse assures the Prophet (sws) and at the same time warns and admonishes the disbelievers too.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For receptive people, the Prophet’s call and the Qur’an awaken truths already present in human nature rather than impose anything from outside.
rows.anchor: it only stirs the treasures found in their nature and brings them before their eyes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with blind hearts cannot equal people whose hearts and minds are radiant, so their fates must differ according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: it is essential that the fate of both be different in accordance with their deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise is the primordial covenant made by every descendant of Adam when souls were summoned before God prior to birth.
rows.anchor: The “promise” refers to the covenant made by every descendent of Adam (sws) when his soul was called in God’s presence before birth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who remember and keep this covenant receive the Qur’an’s reminder; the Prophet should expect no good from those who corrupt their nature and break it.
rows.anchor: they who have this covenant in mind and have not broken it are the ones who will receive reminder from the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God asks people to preserve refers to blood relations, whose rights they fulfill sincerely from the heart rather than for show.
rows.anchor: This refers to blood relations. In other words, just as they give due respect from the bottom of their hearts to the rights of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi cites 76:8–10 as a parallel: feeding others despite need, solely for God, without seeking reward or gratitude, from fear of the Day.
rows.anchor: In verses 8-10 of Sūrah al-Dahr, it is thus stated:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is a significant difference between merely praying and being diligent in prayer.
rows.anchor: It may be noted that there is a world of difference between praying and being

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Formal spending through zakāh is public spending, but discharging zakāh does not remove the need for further charity; secret spending is vital for spiritual growth and self-purification.
rows.anchor: Zakāh comes under spending openly. Secret spending on which depends real spiritual elevation is still needed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repaying evil with good is a general principle, but here it includes spending on those who mistreat them; Qur’an and Hadith stress its weight with God.
rows.anchor: Thus they even spend on those who do not treat them properly.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “abode” denotes the Hereafter, where true success belongs to the righteous.
rows.anchor: real success in the hereafter will be their share.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ideas of polytheism and intercession are baseless because they collapse truth into falsehood and oppression into injustice.
rows.anchor: Those who have invented polytheism and intercession, have created baseless concepts because in this way they equate truth with falsehood and oppression with injustice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the eternal gardens elaborates the successful Hereafter fate stated in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: These are the details of the successful fate of the hereafter mentioned in the previous verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Including relatives in Paradise is conditional on their being worthy; omitting this condition would undermine the system of justice.
rows.anchor: This is a basic condition which if not met will destroy the whole system of justice

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s bounty can unite a person with worthy relatives even if they merit a lower category in Paradise.
rows.anchor: unite a person’s relatives with him even if they are worthy of a lower category in Paradise.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words “how nice is the successful end” are not spoken by angels; they are God’s praise of the high rank attained in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: It is in fact a praise from the Almighty for the high rank they will ultimately receive in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts from the previous verse’s expression to emphasize the majesty of the Hereafter abode.
rows.anchor: Here in order to explain the majesty of the abode of the Hereafter, the words are

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Anbiyā’ pairs with Ṭāhā and opens where that sūrah ended: a warning that Quraysh’s demanded punishment sign is near.
rows.anchor: This sūrah forms a pair with Sūrah Ṭāhā, the previous sūrah. It begins on the same note on which the last sūrah ended.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the end of Ṭāhā, Quraysh were told to wait if they insisted on seeing a punishment sign, since punishment was near.
rows.anchor: if they insist on seeing a sign of the punishment, then they should wait because the punishment is at hand.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Messenger’s advent, Quraysh’s accountability is imminent, yet they remain absorbed in frivolities.
rows.anchor: the time of accountability of the Quraysh is now imminent but they are engrossed in frivolties.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mock the Prophet and revelation, calling him sorcerer, magician, poet, or impostor, or dismissing revelation as wayward dreams.
rows.anchor: Some call him a sorcerer, some a magician, some a poet and an imposter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand miracles from the Prophet like those performed by earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: They demand from him similar miracles as the ones worked by previous prophets.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They regard the world as amusement created to entertain its Creator.
rows.anchor: They regard this world to be a place of amusement created to entertain the creator.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their trust rests on self-created idols that are figments of their imagination.
rows.anchor: All their trust hinges on their self-created idols. The fact is that these are figments of their own imagination.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s prophets have no connection with these imagined idols.
rows.anchor: Prophets of God have nothing to do with them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Where Ṭāhā recounts only Moses, al-Anbiyā’ cites other prophets to highlight Qur’anic teachings.
rows.anchor: In the previous sūrah, only the account of Moses (sws) was cited. In this one, accounts of other prophets are also cited.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah predicts truth’s dominance and the conquest of Makkah, warning Quraysh and giving Muslims glad tidings amid adversity.
rows.anchor: the dominance of the truth and the conquest of Makkah are also predicted in an explicit way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah has three sections: it warns Quraysh, highlights Qur’anic truths through prophetic histories, then returns to the opening warning and their coming fate.
rows.anchor: consists of three large sections. First the Quraysh are clearly warned of their foolish behaviour

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters and their People of the Book supporters delude themselves that they are Abraham’s true custodians and may bar the Prophet and followers from the House.
rows.anchor: they think that it is they who are the real custodians of Abraham’s religion and the House of God and hence have the right to close its doors

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham built the House for worship of the one God and pilgrimage, not for idolatry and polytheism.
rows.anchor: Abraham (sws) never built this House for idolatry and polytheism. On the other hand, they have precisely done this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attention to the real essence of animal sacrifice and Hajj rituals urges Abraham’s legacy claimants to reevaluate their beliefs.
rows.anchor: attention is directed to the real essence of animal sacrifice and other rituals of ḥajj

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claimants have distorted Abraham’s legacy and are bent on expelling those who seek to revive it.
rows.anchor: they have totally distorted his legacy and his teachings. To make matters worse, they are bent upon expelling those who are trying to revive this legacy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 38–41 are Medinan; after migration, Muslims faced the question of what to do if Quraysh blocked their pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: the question arose as to what they should do if they go for ḥajj and the disbelievers try to stop them?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although fighting in sacred months near the House was prohibited even in jāhiliyyah, Quraysh used that sanctity as a shield and Muslims would not breach it without God’s permission.
rows.anchor: waging war in the sacred months and that too within the vicinity of the House of God was regarded as prohibited even in the times of jāhiliyyah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If war becomes inevitable, Muslims may retaliate; this does not violate sacred months but is a holy war to cleanse the House and, if able, liberate it from usurpers.
rows.anchor: This war does not violate the sanctity of the sacred months; in fact, it is a holy war for the cleansing of the House of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating such war as impious would leave monotheistic houses of worship to enemies who could destroy them or turn them into idol centers.
rows.anchor: all houses of worship that have been built for the One God are being consigned to the disbelievers and their accomplices.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims should not hesitate at war or heed opponents’ accusations; despite their small numbers and scarce resources, God will grant them authority in Makkah.
rows.anchor: in spite of their small number and scarcity of resources, God will help them to grant them authority in the land of Makkah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once empowered, Muslims should cleanse the Ḥaram of polytheism and disbelief and restore the purpose for which Abraham settled the land.
rows.anchor: they should cleanse the Ḥaram from the filth of polytheism and disbelief and revive the objectives

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Medinan, these verses are placed in a Makkan sūrah because Quraysh’s illegitimate occupation follows the prior argument and this permission answers prevailing circumstances.
rows.anchor: they were placed here in a Makkan sūrah so that it becomes evident that this permission was given because of the prevailing circumstances.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 42–52 cite historical evidence that warnings delivered by God through messengers always came to pass.
rows.anchor: Evidence from history is cited that the warning meted out by God to various nations through His messengers always materialized.
